title: Anti-HER2 treatment Discontinuation Guided by ctDNA in Patients with HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer with Sustained Disease Control: PHENIX Trial
official: Anti-HER2 treatment Discontinuation Guided by ctDNA in Patients with HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer with Sustained Disease Control: PHENIX Trial
summary: Main objective: To determine the proportion of patients with undetectable MRD by ctDNA (Cohort A), who, after discontinuation of anti-HER2 therapy, remain free from mBC over a two-year follow-up period. Anti-HER2 therapy can be reintroduced upon molecular progression

interventions.name: Perjeta 420 mg concentrate for solution for infusion
Phesgo 1200 mg/600 mg solution for injection

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients (men or women) should be older than 18 years of age
2. Maintenance of endocrine therapy including tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors or fulvestrant for hormone receptor (HR)-positive disease is allowed, as well as concomitant ovarian blockade using Luteinizing Hormone-Releasing Hormone (LHRH) agonists for pre/perimenopausal women or men
3. Patients receiving other endocrine targeted treatments like CDK4/6 inhibitors, PARP inhibitors, everolimus or PI3K pathway inhibitors will be required to stop those treatments at inclusion as well as anti-HER2 therapy
4. Associated bone remodeling therapies are allowed. Patients included in the study may maintain bone remodeling therapies at the investigator’s discretion
5. Patients with no evidence of disease (NED) after surgery, ablation or radiotherapy for any metastatic lesion are eligible if more than 2 years from the last intervention and no evidence of disease progression over the last 3 years
6. Patients need to show they are willing and able to stick to the study rules, like coming to appointments, following the treatment plan, and taking part in all study activities, including follow-ups
7. Patients must have signed a written informed consent form (ICF) prior to any trial specific procedures
8. Confirmed diagnosis of metastatic disease (Stage IV according to AJCC Staging – 8th edition) and histologically proven HER2+ mBC (according to ASCO-CAP guidelines)
9. Patients should be currently receiving first-line anti-HER2 therapy with T alone or TP for a minimum of 36 months with their last dose received within 3 weeks of inclusion
10. Patients should not have any evidence of clinical or radiological progression over the last 3 years. For patients with stable disease or PR the physician should rule out any residual tumor activity in bone scan and/or CT scans at least 12 months before inclusion.
11. Patients require a PET-CT or CT scan and bone scan, as well as mammography (if applicable), to confirm the absence of clinical or radiological progression at the time of inclusion. Patients with radiological PR or SD may be included provided that there is no evidence of active or progressive disease on longitudinal imaging for at least 12 months prior to inclusion. In these participants, eligibility for treatment discontinuation must be confirmed by the treating physician, who will document that the persistent radiological findings are consistent with treated/inactive disease and that residual viable tumor activity cannot reasonably be identified
12. Participants with PR or SD and negative ctDNA/MRD must have no clinically suspicious findings suggestive of active metastatic disease at the time of enrollment. The treating  physician will review the available longitudinal imaging and clinical information before treatment discontinuation and document that there is no evidence of active tumor activity. If residual viable disease cannot reasonably be excluded, the participant will not be eligible for treatment discontinuation. Patients with history of brain metastasis or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis are suitable for the study but require a brain MRI with no evidence of active disease
13. Adequate cardiac, renal, hematologic and liver functions according to local guidelines
14. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test performed within 28 days before inclusion and must comply with the reproductive-safety requirements specified in Section 7.4, including contraception requirements and pregnancy testing during anti-HER2 treatment and before any reintroduction of anti-HER2 treatment.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with ECOG performance status (PS) equal or greater than 2
2. Any evidence of BC progression over the past 3 years or at study entry
3. Patients concurrently using other approved or investigational antineoplastic agents than T, P or endocrine therapies. Targeted agents like PARP-inhibitors, CDK4/6-inhibitors, everolimus or PI3K pathway inhibitors are not allowed (must be stopped at the time of inclusion)
4. Prior history of other malignancies (except for basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin or carcinoma in situ of the cervix) within the last 5 years
5. No associated severe pathologies - “normal” life expectancy in the absence of expected tumor events in the next 2 years
6. Current participation in a prospective study regarding first line treatment with TP. Patients will be allowed to participate if the study is finally closed for active follow-up
